Hi, Please can anyone help with this problem it's driving me crazy.Background - I'm using Jira Cloud, Team Managed Board, I am the admin of the board but not the jira admin.What I want to do - we have book titles that change through production as a name becomes signed off. The book title exists in the Epic Summary, Work Type (Task) Summary, Sub Task Summary and a Book Title Field which is on all of the work Types. Here is the start of my Automation: The Create Variable doesn't work: {{issue.summary.replaceAll("(?i)\\Q{{oldT}}\\E","{{newT}}")}} Here is the set up within my board: So I want to be able to Find all Instances of : A Garden for Grandad Graham in the epic, task, sub task and update it to another name: Gardening Graham. I want to run the manual trigger from the epic. I can't even get the Epic Summary to change. I have this Log: Please please can someone help. I just am stuck on
...
first bit and haven't even got to updating the custom field or the children of the epic. thank you
...
Adding to the suggestions from@Valerie Knapp and I agree a manually triggered rule may not be a sustainable approach to solve your scenario. And also...
...
For smart value expressions, once inside a set of double, curly brackets, additional ones are not needed.
...
Next, automation rule regular expressions cannot include smart values directly. Instead, one needs to create a variable for the regex and then use that in the functions. For example:
...
action: create variable
...
- name: varRegExString
- smart value: your regular expression, with no surrounding quotation marks
...
action: create variable
...
- name: varRegExReplacement
- smart value: your regular expression, with no surrounding quotation marks
...
action: something that needs to use the results...
...
- {{issue.someField.replaceAll(varRegExString, varStringExReplacement)}}
...
Finally, and most importantly, there is no documentation of what is and is not supported for regular expressions in automation rules. Instead, the docs state the implementation is based on Java's Pattern class. This means one needs to experiment to confirm the behavior, such as by:
...
- create the simplest expression that can solve your case
- test that fully, perhaps just writing the results to the audit log rather than changing work items
- when that works, incrementally add to the regex for edge cases, again testing
- when an expression does not work, pause to understand why, and perhaps consider alternatives to using regex in the rule, such as other text functions
...
I would suggest to you that an automation isn't the best solution for this requirement. I think a listener would be better. A listener works as it sounds like it would, it is 'listening' for some change and then you can update other related objects https://www.scriptrunnerhq.com/help/example-scripts/update-multiple-fields-cloud
...
I have understood that when the title of the book is updated, you want to update it everywhere it has been referenced. However, I think it is important that you define a process for in which object the title should be updated, otherwise, I don't see how you wouldn't just be constantly overwriting different titles without any quality control. I appreciate you have this rule as a manual trigger but I think for your internal processes it would make sense to define, ok, this title is outdated, I will update it (as a rule) in the Epic and then the update of the Epic would be the event that triggers the change in the other related objects.
...
If the goal is to replace the text with the user-provided value, wouldn’t it be simpler to just update the fields directly with that value? For example:

...
From what I understood, the problem to be solved is the need to edit the book title in multiple places. Since handling partial text is more complex than replacing the entire text, the simpler approach would be to:
...
Copy the summary once
...
Paste the current summary into the manual trigger field and make the necessary edits

only_yaml = ykeys - jkeys
common = jkeys & ykeys

    ym = ymodels[m]

    for f in price_fields:
        jv = jm.get('cost', {}).get(f, None)
        yv = ym.get('cost', {}).get(f, None)
        if jv != yv:
            if f not in diffs: diffs[f] = {}
            diffs[f]['json'] = jv
            diffs[f]['yaml'] = yv
    
    # Compare limits
    for f in limit_fields:
        jv = jm.get('limit', {}).get(f, None)
        yv = ym.get('limit', {}).get(f, None)
        if jv != yv:
            key = f'limit.{f}'
            if key not in diffs: diffs[key] = {}
            diffs[key]['json'] = jv
            diffs[key]['yaml'] = yv
    
    # Compare context_over_200k tiers
    jt = jm.get('cost', {}).get('tiers', [])
    yt = ym.get('cost', {}).get('tiers', [])
    jco = jm.get('cost', {}).get('context_over_200k', None)
    yco = ym.get('cost', {}).get('context_over_200k', None)
    
    if (jt and not yt) or (not jt and yt):
        diffs['tiers'] = {'json': 'present' if jt else 'absent', 'yaml': 'present' if yt else 'absent'}
    if (jco and not yco) or (not jco and yco):
        diffs['context_over_200k'] = {'json': 'present' if jco else 'absent', 'yaml': 'present' if yco else 'absent'}
    
    if diffs:
        discrepancies.append((m, jm.get('family','?'), diffs))

print(f"JSON models: {len(jkeys)}")
print(f"YAML models: {len(ykeys)}")
print(f"Common: {len(common)}")
print(f"Only in JSON: {sorted(only_json)}")
print(f"Only in YAML: {sorted(only_yaml)}")
print()

    print(f"\n{m} (family: {fam})")
    for k, v in diffs.items():
        print(f"  {k}: JSON={v['json']}, YAML={v['yaml']}")

The file concludes **`whisper-large-v3` is the primary recommendation** for Malayalam ASR on the NVIDIA free tier.

---

## C2. Whisper vs Canary Malayalam Accuracy (Web)

### Canary does NOT support Malayalam

This is the critical finding. The NVIDIA Canary model family (`canary-1b`, `canary-1b-v2`, `canary-1b-flash`) supports exactly **25 languages** — all European plus Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Thai, and Chinese. **Malayalam is not in the set.** The official NVIDIA docs list:

> `ar-AR`, `cs-CZ`, `da-DK`, `de-DE`, `en-GB`, `en-US`, `es-ES`, `es-US`, `fr-CA`, `fr-FR`, `he-IL`, `hi-IN`, `it-IT`, `ja-JP`, `ko-KR`, `nb-NO`, `nl-NL`, `nn-NO`, `pl-PL`, `pt-BR`, `pt-PT`, `ru-RU`, `sv-SE`, `th-TH`, `tr-TR`, `zh-CN`

No `ml` (Malayalam) entry. A direct Whisper-vs-Canary accuracy comparison for Malayalam is therefore **not possible** — Canary simply cannot transcribe Malayalam.

### Whisper Malayalam Accuracy (all available WER numbers)

Since Canary has no Malayalam capability, here is the complete picture for Whisper on Malayalam:

#### Zero-shot (no fine-tuning)

| Model | Dataset | WER | Source |
|-------|---------|-----|--------|
| Whisper-small | FLEURS (without normalization) | **287.4%** | arXiv 2409.02449 |
| Whisper-small | FLEURS (with Whisper normalization) | **135.2%** | arXiv 2409.02449 |
| Whisper-tiny | Common Voice | **154.21%** | kurianbenoy/malayalam_asr_benchmarking |
| Whisper-base | Common Voice | **118.39%** | same |
| Whisper-small | Common Voice | **100.06%** | same |
| Whisper-medium | Common Voice | **127.97%** | same |
| Whisper-large | Common Voice | **125.73%** | same |
| Whisper-large-v2 | Common Voice | **100.26–107.01%** | same |

> WER >100% is common for low-resource languages — insertion errors cause the total error count to exceed the reference word count. Whisper's internal normalization also artificially inflates WER for Indic scripts (see arXiv 2409.02449).

#### Fine-tuned Whisper models for Malayalam (notable results)

| Model | Dataset | WER | CER | Params |
|-------|---------|-----|-----|--------|
| **thennal/whisper-medium-ml** | Common Voice 11.0 (with normalization) | **11.49%** | — | 769M |
| **thennal/whisper-medium-ml** | Common Voice 11.0 (no normalization) | **38.62%** | 7.33% | 769M |
| anuragshas/whisper-large-v2-ml | Common Voice | **24.46%** | 11.64% | 1.54B |
| parambharat/whisper-small-ml | Common Voice | **21.65%** | 11.78% | 244M |
| parambharat/whisper-base-ml | Common Voice | **30.33%** | 16.16% | 72.6M |
| sajilck/whisper-small-malayalam | Common Voice 25 | **37.64%** | — | 244M |
| whisper-medium-ml-high-lr | Vividh-ASR (Global) | **40.85%** | — | 769M |
| whisper-medium-ml-rmft | Vividh-ASR (Global) | **39.64%** | — | 769M |

The best reported result is **`thennal/whisper-medium-ml` at 11.49% WER** (with normalization on Common Voice 11.0). This is a Malayalam-fine-tuned variant of `openai/whisper-medium` and is available on Hugging Face.

#### Whisper-large-v3 specific

The file notes `whisper-large-v3` is available on the NVIDIA free tier and supports Malayalam. No specific published FLEURS WER for `large-v3` on Malayalam was found in this search, but:
- Whisper-large-v3 on FLEURS achieves sub-10% WER on ~30 languages
- Languages with small training corpora (like Malayalam) typically see **>>30% WER** zero-shot
- The closest Dravidian language benchmarks for Whisper-large-v3 FLEURS: **Tamil 29.4%** (Vocova.blog, 2026)

---

### On the broader Whisper-vs-Canary comparison (languages both support)

For context, on languages where both models are available:

| Benchmark | Canary-1B-v2 | Whisper-large-v3 |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| FLEURS-25 Langs (avg WER) | **8.40%** | ~9.9% |
| CoVoST-13 Langs (avg WER) | **8.85%** | — |
| MLS-6 Langs (avg WER) | **7.27%** | — |
| HuggingFace ASR Leaderboard avg | ~7.15% | ~7.16% |
| English ASR avg | **6.50%** | 7.16% |
| Inference speed (RTFx) | **749×** | ~100× |

Canary generally matches or slightly beats Whisper on the languages they share, and runs 7–10× faster. **But this does not apply to Malayalam because Canary does not support it.**

---

## C3. Verdict

**Whisper (fine-tuned) is the only viable option for Malayalam ASR among NVIDIA free models. Canary does not support Malayalam at all and cannot be compared.**

| Factor | Whisper-large-v3 | NVIDIA Canary |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|

1. **All 144 models are free on build.nvidia.com.** The "free" designation in the source document refers to the Developer preview tier — every model listed costs $0 to use within the ~40 RPM rate limit. There is no model in the catalog that is paywalled on the development tier.

2. **Free tier = all models, not a subset.** Unlike OpenAI or Anthropic where some models are always paid, NVIDIA's build.nvidia.com makes the entire catalog available under the same free Developer terms. You don't need to wonder "is model X free" — they all are.

3. **Production is where payment starts.** The free-vs-paid distinction is **by deployment mode, not by model**:

   - **NIM production hosted endpoints** → paid (custom per-token)
   - **Self-hosted NIM containers** → paid (NVIDIA AI Enterprise ~$4,500/GPU/year)
